examples.title: Build and evaluate a postfix tree
examples.explanationHtml: The first popped tree becomes the right child. The expression is (8-2)*3, so its value is 18.

examples.title: Parentheses preserve the shape
examples.explanationHtml: The tree groups 2*3 before subtraction. Infix prints (8-(2*3)), while preorder produces -8*23.

examples.title: Reject an operator without two children
examples.explanationHtml: The plus sign finds only one subtree. The parser frees that subtree and reports invalid rather than popping past the stack.

practice.title: Count expression operators
practice.statementHtml: Read a line of at most 15 symbols: digits 0..9, spaces, and binary + - *. Print Postfix (up to 15 symbols, digits and +-*): then operators=C, or invalid for a malformed expression.
hints: Only internal nodes count as operators.

practice.title: Convert postfix to prefix
practice.statementHtml: Read postfix using at most 15 digits, spaces and + - *. Print Postfix (up to 15 symbols, digits and +-*): then prefix: followed immediately by preorder symbols, or invalid.
hints: Build before printing so malformed input produces no partial conversion.

practice.title: Count expression leaves
practice.statementHtml: Read postfix with at most 15 symbols, using digits, spaces and binary + - *. Print Postfix (up to 15 symbols, digits and +-*): then operands=C or invalid.
hints: A full expression tree has one more leaf than internal nodes.

practice.title: Mirror subtraction by swapping children
practice.statementHtml: Read postfix with at most 15 digits, spaces and + - *. Print Postfix (up to 15 symbols, digits and +-*): then infix: and value=V after swapping children at every operator, or invalid.
hints: Subtraction changes sign when operands swap; multiplication keeps operand order irrelevant.

quiz.prompt: For postfix 82-, which popped subtree is the right operand?
quiz.explanation: The later operand is on top of the subtree stack.

quiz.prompt: Which traversal gives a binary expression tree postfix form?
quiz.explanation: Children must be emitted before their operator.

quiz.prompt: How many subtree roots should remain after valid postfix parsing?
quiz.explanation: Every binary operator replaces two roots with one combined root.

quiz.prompt: Why print parentheses around each internal expression?
options: To turn every operator into addition
To preserve grouping independently of precedence
quiz.explanation: Inorder symbols alone can represent a different expression.

options: Plus has only one available operand
Plus cannot be stored in a char
quiz.explanation: A binary operator requires two roots before popping.

quiz.prompt: What tree shape must binary operators produce?
options: Every node has exactly one child
Every operator node has exactly two children
quiz.explanation: The parser creates both operand links together.

quiz.prompt: What does an evaluation routine do at a digit leaf?
quiz.explanation: Subtracting the character code for zero converts a digit to its integer value.

quiz.prompt: The postfix minus pops right before left. Which difference is computed?
quiz.explanation: The left operand is 8 and the right operand is 2, giving 6.

quiz.prompt: Each binary operator reduces the root-stack size by one. What final size does 23+4* produce?
quiz.explanation: Three operands add three roots and two operators remove one root each, leaving one.

quiz.prompt: Digit leaves use character subtraction. What value does leaf 7 return?
quiz.explanation: C guarantees contiguous decimal digit codes, so subtracting zero yields seven.

examQuestions.question: Draw the tree for postfix 82-3* and give its infix, prefix and value.
examQuestions.answerHtml:
*
     / \
    -   3
   / \
  8   2

Fully parenthesized infix is ((8-2)*3). Prefix is *-823. Evaluate the left minus as six, then multiply by three, giving 18. The minus node receives right operand 2 before left operand 8 when popping.

examQuestions.question: Describe cleanup when postfix parsing ends with several independent roots.
examQuestions.answerHtml: Each stack entry owns a disjoint complete subtree. A valid expression requires exactly one entry; otherwise repeatedly pop a root and dispose its left subtree, right subtree and root record. Operator allocation occurs before removing operand owners, so allocation failure can use the same cleanup path without losing records.

examQuestions.question: Why can inorder without parentheses change an expression? Use 823*- as the example.
examQuestions.answerHtml: The tree has minus at the root, leaf 8 on the left and multiplication of 2 and 3 on the right. Its infix is (8-(2*3)), value 2. A different tree for 82-3* would also give unparenthesized symbols 8-2*3, but its stored grouping yields 18. Parentheses distinguish these shapes rather than relying on the printed token order alone.
